title: Introduce stream preflight + runtime deferred-strictness toggle for JSON schema enforcement
author: Eloise Park
release_notes: Adds optional stream preflight handshake and runtime toggle for deferred strict schema enforcement to improve streaming stability and provide clearer OpenAI-compatible error mapping.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight stream preflight check and a runtime 'deferred_strict' toggle for JSON schema enforcement on streaming responses. The goal is to reduce premature hard-fails during streaming, improve developer UX for structured outputs, and provide deterministic error mapping to the OpenAI compatibility layer.

Motivation: We have observed a class of customer issues where downstream consumers (SDKs and frameworks expecting strict JSON output) trigger failures mid-stream due to transient tokenization/formatting issues or minor schema ordering differences. Completely relaxing validation is undesirable because it hides real regressions.

The proposed approach:
1) Stream preflight: before switching into full streaming mode the runtime performs a small, non-blocking preflight that asks the model to emit an example or a compact schema test payload (bounded length). This verifies the model variant and prompt produce a streamable JSON shape without introducing meaningful latency for successful calls. If preflight fails, the system returns an actionable error early with OpenAI-compatible error codes and a short diagnostic hint.

2) Deferred strictness toggle: add a per-request flag (response_format.deferred_strict = true/false) that permits the runtime to accept soft schema deviations during streaming and attempt post-stream reconciliation. When deferred_strict=true, the runtime will:
- continue streaming even if incremental chunks can't be immediately schema-validated, while buffering minimal checkpoints (parseable prefixes, KV-cache anchors)
- attempt a post-stream strict validation step using the accumulated tokens and, if necessary, emit a structured parse error with exact byte offsets and recovery hints
- optionally offer an automated rollback to the last-known-good model variant (configurable via routing policy) for immediate fallback.

3) Tool-call fence during preflight: for models configured to call tools, the preflight signals to tool-schedulers that the first tool call should be gated until a successful preflight; this reduces spurious tool invocations triggered by malformed early tokens.

Design details:
- New runtime component: StreamPreflightManager (lightweight, per-request). Implemented as a non-blocking probe that requests a compact sample response (max 512 tokens) with response_format=schematest; for most LLMs this is a single-turn probe that completes in under 50ms added overhead in well-provisioned paths.
- Checkpointing: introduce minimal stream checkpoints (parseable prefix + KV anchor) to allow partial post-hoc validation without re-running the full generation. Checkpoints are memory-bounded and evicted for long-running streams.
- OpenAI compat mapping: errors from preflight or post-stream strict validation are mapped to openai.error types (e.g., invalid_request_error, rate_limit_exceeded, content_filter) and contain an extra 'redwood_hint' field with suggested remediation (prompt fix, model variant switch, or toggle).
- Telemetry: emit new metrics: preflight_success_rate, deferred_strict_postfail_count, preflight_latency_p50/p95, toolcall_gated_count, and an event with validation_diagnostics (redacted).
- Configuration surface: API-level: response_format.deferred_strict (boolean), response_format.preflight (auto|always|never), and a new route-level default in console. Default behavior: preflight=auto, deferred_strict=false to preserve existing strict behavior; enterprise customers can opt in per-route.

Backwards compatibility:
- Default is no behavior change.
- When using OpenAI-compat mode, error payloads include compatibility mappings so client libraries expecting OpenAI error shapes can parse them.

Tests:
- unit: parser/stream-preflight manager, checkpoint eviction, mapping tests (added 47 unit tests)
- integration: e2e streaming with preflight enabled for GPT-style model shim and for one quantized Llama variant; validated under small and burst loads
- perf: benchmark shows median added latency for successful calls with auto preflight is +12ms on our benchmark lab.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/stream/preflight_manager.py: new component with detailed logging and metrics
- runtime/stream/checkpoint_store.py: lightweight write-through checkpoints
- runtime/validation/schema_postprocessor.py: post-stream strict validation and error formatting
- api/response/handler.py: plumbing for response_format flags and preflight orchestration
- openai_compat/mapper.py: map Redwood validation errors to OpenAI error shapes
- console/schema-settings.md: UI/instructions for route-level toggle
- sdk/python/redwood/responses.py: expose response_format.deferred_strict flag in Python SDK
- tests/{unit,integration}/...: new and updated tests

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-4782)
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Telemetry and metrics emitted with feature gates
- [x] SDK flag surfaced in Python SDK and validated in integration tests
- [x] Console text and defaults updated

Commits summary: - feat(stream): add StreamPreflightManager and probe orchestration - feat(validation): add deferred post-stream strict validator + diagnostics - feat(api): add response_format flags and routing fallback hooks - feat(openai-compat): error mapping for preflight/postfail cases - test: add unit and integration tests - docs: console and SDK usage

Review conversation summary: - Ravi: "Preflight adds value but I'm worried about the interaction with burst autoscaling; can this flood model slots?" Reply: "Preflight uses a lightweight sample probe and respects routing limits; added a per-route preflight_rate_limit default to avoid bursts (see preflight_manager)." - Sofia: "We need clear telemetry to differentiate real schema regressions from tokenizer noise." Reply: "Added deferred_strict_postfail_count and validation_diagnostics event; diagnostics are redacted but include token offsets and example failing prefixes." - Liam: "SDK change looks fine; add a short example in the quickstart." Reply: "Added Python example and an update to redwood-quickstarts/snippets/streaming_schema.md" - QA: found a flaky test in integration that assumed no preflight on legacy routes; fixed by guarding tests behind feature flag. CI: initial run failed on flaky integration/test_stream_resume.py, rerun passed. Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and a green CI run.

Impact and followups: - We expect a net reduction in mid-stream hard-fails for structured-output workflows; customers using strict streaming can opt into deferred_strict to ease migrations.
- Followups: automated canary that toggles deferred_strict for a small % of traffic (ENG-4791), and a post-deploy job to backfill telemetry into dashboards.
